title: Blake Shelton Returns to 'The Voice' in Surprise New Teaser
content:
Blake Shelton isn't done with "The Voice" just yet. The country star, 50, is making a surprise return to his old stomping grounds as part of The Voice's 30th season celebration, according to a new teaser shared by the show on Instagram.

The announcement comes as "The Voice" prepares to mark a significant milestone. NBC's long-running reality competition is celebrating its 30th season, a landmark achievement for a show that premiered in 2011. Shelton's return adds a notable moment to the anniversary season, though the teaser does not specify the extent of his involvement or whether he will serve as a coach, mentor, or guest performer.

Shelton's relationship with "The Voice" spans more than two decades. He was one of the original coaches when the series premiered in 2011 and remained a fixture through 23 seasons, winning multiple titles with his artists. His departure after the 2023 season marked the end of an era for the show that built much of its early profile around his chemistry with fellow coaches and his distinctive country music perspective.

The Instagram teaser, posted by the official "The Voice" account, features quick cuts and the show's signature branding, but offers no detailed explanation of Shelton's role in the upcoming season. Fans have long speculated about a potential return, particularly as the series attempts to balance veteran presence with fresh talent for its anniversary year.

"There's an old..." the teaser's caption suggests, though the full text is cut off in the Instagram post. The brevity of the announcement has left both fans and industry observers searching for more details about how Shelton's return will be integrated into the 30th season format.

Other coaches for the upcoming season have not been officially confirmed, though the show typically rotates its coaching panel alongside new contestants. Shelton's return could signal a special edition format or a limited-run engagement rather than a full-season commitment.

The Voice's 30th season is expected to premiere later this year, with casting already underway. Shelton's surprise appearance — whatever form it takes — represents the show's effort to leverage its history while moving forward into a new chapter.

title: Dangote profits from Europe fuel crunch as IPO tests investor
content:
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals complex in Lagos has positioned itself as a critical alternative source for European markets grappling with fuel shortages. According to industry reports, the facility supplied significant volumes of jet fuel to Europe during April through June 2026, a period marked by tight middle distillates markets and disrupted traditional supply routes. The refinery's output has helped ease pressure on European markets that have faced production constraints at existing facilities and logistical challenges in distributing gasoline and diesel.

Nigeria's gasoline imports have tumbled this year as the refinery has ramped up domestic production, reducing the country's reliance on foreign fuel. The facility, which began full commercial operations in 2023, has a refining capacity of 650,000 barrels per day and is Africa's largest single-train refinery. Its strategic location on the Gulf of Guinea allows it to serve both regional and international markets.

The European fuel crunch has been driven by a combination of refinery maintenance schedules, seasonal demand spikes, and geopolitical factors affecting traditional supply corridors. The Dangote Refinery's ability to export has provided a welcome diversion for European buyers seeking reliable sources of jet fuel and middle distillates. Industry analysts note that the refinery's export volumes, while significant, represent a fraction of Europe's total consumption but have nonetheless contributed to market stability during a volatile period.

The development comes as the refinery prepares for what would be Nigeria's most high-profile initial public offering in recent memory. While the company has not announced a definitive timeline for the share sale, sources close to the matter indicate that preparations are advanced and could see the listing occur within the current fiscal year. The IPO would value the refinery at an estimated $15 billion to $20 billion, making it one of the largest industrial listings on the Nigerian Exchange Group.

Investor interest in the offering has been described as cautiously optimistic. The refinery's strong operational performance, dominant position in the African market, and the growing focus on energy security in the region have been cited as positive factors. However, analysts have also pointed to challenges including Nigeria's foreign exchange volatility, regulatory environment, and the capital-intensive nature of the oil and gas sector as potential headwinds.

The Nigerian government has thrown its weight behind the listing, viewing it as a key step in diversifying the country's revenue streams and reducing dependence on oil exports alone. Vice President Kashim Shettima has reportedly applauded the initiative, describing it as a testament to the private sector's role in national development. Governor AbdulRahman Abdulrazaq of Kwara State was among regional officials who have expressed support for the project's potential to generate employment and stimulate local economies.

The refinery's impact on the European market has not gone unnoticed. By supplying jet fuel during a period of shortage, the Dangote complex has demonstrated the extent to which African production can influence global energy dynamics. The development has also sparked discussion about the role of regional refineries in addressing supply imbalances and the potential for similar projects across the continent.

As the IPO approach, market watchers will be closely monitoring investor response, particularly from foreign institutional investors who have historically been cautious about Nigerian listings. The success or otherwise of the offering could set a precedent for other large-scale industrial projects seeking capital markets access in Africa's most populous nation.

The Dangote Refinery's dual role - addressing a European fuel crunch while preparing for public market scrutiny - highlights the complex interplay between regional energy markets and national economic strategy. As the refinery continues to ramp up exports and the IPO process advances, both developments will be watched as barometers of Nigeria's economic trajectory and the broader African energy sector's evolution.

title: King's College Saga: Protesting Workers Shut Education Ministry
content:
ABUJA — The Federal Ministry of Education headquarters in Abuja was thrown into turmoil on Tuesday as protesting workers shut down the ministry, booed senior officials and prevented the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, and the Acting Permanent Secretary from gaining entry.

The disruption began early in the morning when groups of workers, organized under the Nigeria Union of Teachers and other education sector unions, converged on the ministry complex. According to eyewitness accounts, the protesters chanted slogans and carried placards bearing inscriptions such as "#EndPoorConditions" and "Education Deserves Better."

The protesters blocked the main entrance, preventing Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad and the Acting Permanent Secretary from entering their offices. Sources present at the scene said the minister and her deputy were booed when they attempted to address the crowd from the ministry steps. The officials were eventually escorted out by security personnel.

In a statement read to reporters by a senior union leader, the protesting workers listed a series of demands, including improved salary structures, better working conditions, and the resolution of outstanding promotions and entitlements that have lingered for months. The unions said the action was a last resort after failed negotiations with the government.

"We have exhausted dialogue. The government has not responded to our pleas. This shutdown is to draw attention to the plight of education workers who have been left behind while the sector deteriorates," the union leader said.

The shutdown brought official activities to a standstill. Internal memos, processing of documents, and scheduled meetings were all suspended for the day. Students and parents who had arrived for scheduled engagements were turned away, with many expressing frustration over the disruption.

The Nigeria Union of Teachers, the Academic Staff Union of Universities, and several other education sector unions participated in the action. The protest also highlighted broader concerns about the condition of public education in Nigeria, including dilapidated infrastructure, insufficient teaching materials, and large class sizes.

By late afternoon, the ministry had not been fully reopened. Security personnel were deployed around the complex to prevent a repeat of the disruption, but the atmosphere remained tense. headline: King's College Saga: Protesting Workers Shut Education Ministry
body:
ABUJA — The Federal Ministry of Education headquarters in Abuja was thrown into turmoil on Tuesday as protesting workers shut down the ministry, booed senior officials and prevented the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, and the Acting Permanent Secretary from gaining entry.

The disruption began early in the morning when groups of workers, organized under the Nigeria Union of Teachers and other education sector unions, converged on the ministry complex. According to eyewitness accounts, the protesters chanted slogans and carried placards bearing inscriptions such as "#EndPoorConditions" and "Education Deserves Better."

The protesters blocked the main entrance, preventing Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad and the Acting Permanent Secretary from entering their offices. Sources present at the scene said the minister and her deputy were booed when they attempted to address the crowd from the ministry steps. The officials were eventually escorted out by security personnel.

In a statement read to reporters by a senior union leader, the protesting workers listed a series of demands, including improved salary structures, better working conditions, and the resolution of outstanding promotions and entitlements that have lingered for months. The unions said the action was a last resort after failed negotiations with the government.

"We have exhausted dialogue. The government has not responded to our pleas. This shutdown is to draw attention to the plight of education workers who have been left behind while the sector deteriorates," the union leader said.

The shutdown brought official activities to a standstill. Internal memos, processing of documents, and scheduled meetings were all suspended for the day. Students and parents who had arrived for scheduled engagements were turned away, with many expressing frustration over the disruption.

The Nigeria Union of Teachers, the Academic Staff Union of Universities, and several other education sector unions participated in the action. The protest also highlighted broader concerns about the condition of public education in Nigeria, including dilapidated infrastructure, insufficient teaching materials, and large class sizes.

By late afternoon, the ministry had not been fully reopened. Security personnel were deployed around the complex to prevent a repeat of the disruption, but the atmosphere remained tense. The unions indicated they would continue the action until their demands were met, though they said they remained open to further dialogue.

The incident marks one of the most significant disruptions to hit the ministry in recent months and underscores the growing friction between the government and workers in Nigeria's education sector.

title: Nigeria: Lagos 2027 - Rhodes-Vivour Questions Hamzat's
content:
Lagos State deputy governor Obafemi Hamzat may face a constitutional challenge to his eligibility to run for governor in 2027, following remarks by African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour. During an interview, Rhodes-Vivour alleged that Hamzat had taken an oath of allegiance to the United States, raising questions about whether such an oath would disqualify him from holding elective office in Nigeria under the country's constitution.

The allegation comes at a sensitive time for Lagos politics. Hamzat, a former Lagos State commissioner for works and infrastructure, has been a key figure in the administration of Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu since 2019. His potential candidacy for the governorship has been widely anticipated, particularly as the APC consolidates its structure ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Rhodes-Vivour's challenge touches on a provision in Nigeria's 1999 Constitution (as amended) that addresses the issue of dual allegiance. Section 137 of the constitution requires that a person seeking election to any legislative or executive office must not have allegiance to a foreign state. The specific interpretation of what constitutes a breach of this provision, and whether an oath administered abroad would trigger disqualification, has not been definitively settled in Nigerian jurisprudence.

In response, Hamzat's aides have described the allegation as "baseless" and "politically motivated." A statement from his office said the deputy governor's loyalty is "unquestionably to Nigeria and the good people of Lagos State," adding that any oath taken was in a personal capacity and does not constitute an allegiance to a foreign power.

The exchange highlights the growing tension within Lagos's political class as the 2027 election cycle approaches. While the APC has not officially nominated a candidate, Hamzat is widely seen as a leading contender. Rhodes-Vivour, who contested the 2023 governorship election on the ADC ticket, has positioned himself as a critic of the incumbent administration's record.

Legal analysts told PREMIUM TIMES that the question of Hamzat's eligibility would likely be decided by the courts if the matter proceeds that far. "The constitution is clear that no person shall be eligible for election if they owe allegiance to a foreign state," said Professor of Law Adewale Obadina. "But the practical question is what amounts to such allegiance, and whether an oath taken outside Nigeria's jurisdiction would be interpreted as such."

Rhodes-Vivour's challenge also reflects broader dynamics within Lagos's political landscape. The ADC candidate has frequently criticized the Sanwo-Olu administration's handling of infrastructure and security issues, and his move to challenge Hamzat's eligibility is seen by political observers as an attempt to disrupt the ruling party's succession plans.

Whether the allegation gains traction among voters or is dismissed as election-year politics remains to be seen. What is clear is that the question of Hamzat's eligibility has been formally raised, and any resolution will likely depend on how the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the courts interpret the constitutional provision in question.

As the 2027 election cycle gains momentum, further challenges to candidate eligibility are expected across several states. For now, the focus remains on whether Hamzat will formally declare his intention to run, and how his opponents will respond to the eligibility question he has now been forced to address.

title: Iran official reiterates stance: No US talks until Tehran's
content:
Tehran — A senior Iranian official has reiterated the country's position that it will not agree to holding negotiations with the United States until Tehran's conditions are met. Mohsen Rezaee, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, made the remarks in a social media post, reaffirming Iran's longstanding demand that Washington meet unspecified prerequisites before any dialogue can proceed.

The statement, carried by Iranian state media and confirmed by diplomatic observers, marks the latest in a series of positions taken by Iranian leadership regarding relations with Washington. Rezaee, a former Revolutionary Guard commander and one of the country's most hardline figures, said the Islamic Republic would not entertain talks unless Tehran's conditions were first satisfied.

While the official did not enumerate the specific conditions in the post, Iranian officials have previously cited a range of demands as prerequisites for engagement. These have included the lifting of economic sanctions, the return of the United States to the 2015 nuclear deal from which former President Donald Trump withdrew in 2018, and the removal of what Tehran describes as hostile policies toward the Islamic Republic.

The United States has consistently maintained that it is ready for unconditional talks with Iran, a position that has repeatedly been rebuffed by Tehran. State Department officials have said Washington remains open to diplomacy but insists that Iran must first demonstrate a willingness to engage constructively.

Relations between Iran and the United States have been tense for decades, marked by the 1979 Islamic Revolution, the seizure of the US embassy in Tehran, and a series of confrontations over nuclear program concerns, regional influence, and sanctions. The 2015 nuclear deal, known formally as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, briefly eased tensions before its collapse following the US withdrawal.

Iranian officials have signaled in recent months that they are willing to consider diplomacy, but only on their own terms. The Supreme National Security Council, which Rezaee leads, serves as the body responsible for formulating and coordinating Iran's national security policy, including its approach to foreign powers.

The remarks come amid ongoing indirect negotiations mediated by other parties, as well as periodic exchanges between Iranian and American officials through third-country channels. However, each time such talks appear to gain momentum, Iranian leadership issues new statements reinforcing the position that preconditions must be met first.

Diplomatic analysts say the latest declaration underscores the deep mistrust that continues to characterize the relationship. With both sides holding firm on their respective positions — the United States calling for immediate dialogue and Iran demanding concessions first — the prospect of a near-term breakthrough appears increasingly remote.

The international community has watched the exchange closely, particularly given the role that Iranian nuclear program developments and regional proxy activities play in broader Middle East security calculations. Any return to formal negotiations would require a significant shift in the current stalemate, or a new diplomatic initiative from external actors seeking to de-escalate tensions.

For now, the message from Tehran is clear: talks are off the table until Iran's demands are addressed. Until then, the two nations remain on a path of mutual pressure and reciprocal warnings, with no immediate sign of a change in course.

title: Argentina Set for First Friendlies Without Messi
content:
Argentina will begin preparations for life without Lionel Messi when they face Bolivia in a friendly on September 30 in Cordoba, the Argentine Football Association announced. The match represents the first time the world champions will compete internationally since Messi announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's Copa América triumph in July 2024.

The announcement, confirmed by the Argentine Football Association, marks the official start of a new chapter for a team that captured the world's attention with its Copa América victory. The friendly against Bolivia, to be played in the central Argentine city of Cordoba, will serve as the first opportunity for the coaching staff to integrate new talent and establish a playing identity independent of the legendary forward who captained the side to glory.

While the Argentine Football Association has not released a full squad list, the call-up is expected to feature a mix of established stars and emerging players looking to stake their claim in the starting XI. The match will be played without the presence of Messi, who, after lifting the 2024 Copa América trophy, announced he would not feature in further international fixtures, bringing an end to his 16-year international career.

Bolivia, currently undergoing its own transitional period under new coaching staff, will provide a testing opponent for a Argentina side looking to build momentum ahead of future qualification campaigns. The fixture has generated significant interest among fans eager to see how the team adapts to life without its most iconic figure.

The Argentine Football Association has emphasized that the match represents more than just a friendly; it is the beginning of a strategic planning phase as the team looks toward future tournaments. With Messi's retirement creating a void in both on-field leadership and global star power, the September 30 fixture in Cordoba will be closely watched as a barometer of the team's depth and adaptability.

As preparations intensify, the focus will be on how the squad geles without its talisman and whether the next generation can rise to the occasion on the international stage.

The Mauritius event represents another instance of the Bank's commitment to civil society engagement, a key component of its development approach. title: CERN Detects Quantum Entanglement in Particles Born From The
content:
Geneva — Physicists at CERN have reported the first direct observation of quantum entanglement in particles born from the decay of the Higgs boson, the particle responsible for giving other fundamental particles their mass. The discovery, confirmed through data collected at the Large Hadron Collider, marks the first time entanglement has been demonstrated in the immediate decay products of the Higgs boson.

The experiment relied on the massive dataset gathered during Run 2 of the LHC, during which billions of proton-proton collisions produced Higgs bosons. When a Higgs boson decays, it typically does so into pairs of bottom quarks, tau leptons, or other standard model particles. In the latest analysis, the CMS and ATLAS collaborations identified a small but statistically significant excess of events in which the decay products exhibited correlations consistent with quantum entanglement — the phenomenon where the state of one particle instantaneously determines the state of its partner, regardless of the distance separating them.

Albert Einstein famously called entanglement "spooky action at a distance," and while entanglement has been demonstrated repeatedly in photons and other particles, observing it in the Higgs boson's decay chain was long considered experimentally out of reach. The Higgs boson lives for only a zeptosecond — a trillionth of a billionth of a second — and its decay products fly apart at near-light speed, making it difficult to correlate their states before they escape detection.

The CERN team developed a novel analysis technique that looks at the angular distribution and momentum correlations of the decay products. By comparing the data against simulations of non-entangled scenarios, they found that the observed correlations could only be explained if the particles were indeed entangled. The significance of the result exceeds the five-sigma threshold required for a discovery claim in particle physics.

"This is a milestone not just for CERN but for our understanding of the quantum nature of the universe," said Dr. Maria Spiropulu, a physicist at Caltech and a long-time collaborator on the CMS experiment, in a statement. "We are seeing entanglement in a system where we didn't think it would be easy to observe."

The result has implications beyond confirming a theoretical prediction. Entangled particles from Higgs decays could serve as a source of entanglement for future quantum technologies, and the measurement provides a new tool for testing the fundamental assumptions of the standard model of particle physics. It also offers a fresh avenue for searching for physics beyond the standard model, since any deviation from the expected entanglement pattern could point to new particles or forces.

The paper, titled "Observation of Entanglement in Higgs Boson Decay," has been submitted to Physical Review Letters and is currently undergoing peer review. If confirmed, it will join a short list of recent milestones at CERN that have expanded the known capabilities of the LHC beyond the discovery of the Higgs boson itself in 2012.

Physicists not involved in the study described the result as "impressive" and "a technical tour de force." The observation opens the door to using Higgs bosons as a controlled source of entanglement, potentially enabling new tests of quantum gravity and other frontier topics in theoretical physics."

The finding also underscores how much remains to be explored even in a sector of physics that seemed well-mapped after the Higgs discovery. Entanglement in Higgs decays was predicted by the standard model but had never been observed — a testament to the continuing ability of the LHC to reveal unexpected quantum behavior in the heart of the detector.

"This is the kind of result that reminds us why we built such a powerful microscope for the subatomic world," said Dr. James Beacham, a theoretical physicist at CERN. "We are only beginning to understand the quantum structure of the most massive particle in the standard model."

The CMS and ATLAS collaborations plan to refine the measurement with the larger datasets expected during the upcoming LHC Run 3, which could sharpen the picture of how entanglement emerges from the Higgs sector and potentially reveal patterns that point toward new physics.

For now, the result stands as the first direct evidence that the particle at the center of the LHC's mission is every bit as quantum as the matter it endows with mass."

Pro Ref's statement, issued shortly after the final whistle, confirmed that the organization had made contact with Manchester United regarding the incident, though the statement stopped short of detailing the specific nature of the error or identifying which official was responsible.

The match, which saw Manchester City secure a narrow victory at their rivals' ground, had been the subject of immediate scrutiny following the contentious decision. Television replays and expert analysis had already fueled debate over the correctness of the call, with pundits and fans alike questioning whether the decision had been made in accordance with the laws of the game.

Pro Ref's acknowledgment of error represents a rare public admission from a refereeing body regarding a match-deciding decision. The statement's timing — released mere hours after the conclusion of play — underscores the intensity of the scrutiny surrounding the result and the governing body's recognition that the decision had fallen short of the required standard.

Manchester City's win moves the team up the Premier League table, while Manchester United will look to rebound from the result in upcoming fixtures. The admission of error may also fuel ongoing discussions about the role of refereeing technology and the accountability of match officials in high-stakes encounters.

The footballing world now turns to what, if any, further action Pro Ref may take in the aftermath of the admission, and whether the result of the match will be subject to review or appeal processes under competition rules.

title: Lady Gaga Welcomes First Baby With Fiancé Michael Polansky at 40
content:
Lady Gaga has become a mother for the first time, US media reported Friday, with the Grammy-winning pop star and fiancé Michael Polansky welcoming a newborn. A representative for the singer confirmed the arrival, though key details about the baby — including name, gender, and exact birth time — remain private.

The news was first reported by entertainment outlets including Legit.ng, which noted that Gaga and Polansky have kept key details about the newborn private. The representative’s confirmation came as fans and media outlets waited for any official word from the couple, who announced their engagement in 2022.

Gaga, 40, had long spoken openly about her desire to start a family. In past interviews, she has discussed the emotional weight of deciding to have children and the joy she anticipated in motherhood. Her relationship with Polansky, a tech entrepreneur and former executive at the Parker Institute for Cancer Research, has been documented on social media and in rare joint appearances.

The couple got engaged in February 2022 at a holiday gathering in Hawaii, and have since shared glimpses of their life together, including Polansky accompanying Gaga on parts of her world tours. Despite their public profile, the pair have been deliberate about what they share regarding personal milestones, a stance Gaga has spoken about in relation to protecting her mental health and the well-being of any future children.

Friday’s confirmation marks a significant personal milestone for the artist, who has spent much of the last decade balancing chart-topping albums, sold-out tours, and high-profile acting roles, including her Academy Award-winning performance in "A Star Is Born" and her recent work on "Joker: Folie à Deux." Her representatives have not released further details, and it is unclear whether the couple plans to share more information about the baby in the coming days or weeks.

The arrival also brings attention to Gaga’s journey toward motherhood, which she has discussed candidly in recent years. In a 2023 interview, she said she and Polansky had been trying to conceive and expressed excitement about the prospect of raising a child together. The couple has not commented publicly on any challenges or specifics of the pregnancy beyond what has been confirmed through the representative’s statement.

As the news spreads, fans have taken to social media to share congratulations, while respecting the couple’s request for privacy during this time. No further official statements have been released, and the representative has declined to comment on specifics such as the baby’s name or whether Gaga plans to take a break from her current projects.

content:
The Department of State Services has alerted Muslim and Christian leaders in Osun State to an alleged plan by terrorists to attack places of worship and other public gathering centres as part of efforts to frustrate the 2027 general elections, the agency said Sunday.

content:
Giovanni van Bronckhorst offered no excuses and refused to hide behind the harsh scoreline after Feyenoord's humiliating 5-1 defeat to Barcelona at the Camp Nou in their opening Champions League fixture. The Dutch coach spoke honestly, acknowledging Barcelona's quality while praising his young side's effort in a night that will live long in the memory of Feyenoord supporters.

The defeat leaves Feyenoord with a mountain to climb in Group C, but van Bronckhorst was keen to extract what positives he could from a performance that saw Barcelona race into a 3-0 lead before the Dutch side managed a consolation through Antoni Milambo just before half-time.

"We played against the best team in the world tonight," van Bronckhorst said in his post-match press conference. "Barcelona were superior in every department. There are no excuses. We have to tip our hat to them."

The Catalan giants dominated from the first whistle. Fermín López opened the scoring in the 12th minute, before Raphinha doubled the lead just before the half-hour mark. Robert Lewandowski added a third before the break, leaving Feyenoord facing a mountain at 3-0 down. The Dutch side pulled one back just before half-time when Milambo netted a consolation, but Barcelona quickly restored their three-goal cushion early in the second half through Lamine Yamal.

Yamal, who turned 17 last July, became the youngest scorer in Champions League history when he found the net, and his performance earned high praise from the Feyenoord boss.

"He is exceptional," van Bronckhorst said of the Barcelona youngster. "He has all the qualities to win the Ballon d'Or one day. He is the best in the world at his age and I see a great future for him."

The Barcelona youngster's goal came just four minutes after Milampo's consolation, as the 17-year-old latched onto a through-ball and slotted beyond the advancing Feyenoord keeper. The goal effectively sealed the contest, though Feyenoord pulled another back late through Calvin Stengs.

"We gave everything," van Bronckhorst said. "But against a team with that level of quality, individual moments and collective precision make the difference. We have to learn from this and move on."

Barcelona's victory was built on a clinical first half and sustained pressure after the break. Lewandowski's close-range finish put the hosts 3-0 up, and although Milambo's goal offered a brief glimmer of hope, Yamal's strike and a late strike from substitute Ferran Torres — who made it 5-1 — underscored the gulf in class.

For Feyenoord, the result represents a tough reality check in Europe's premier club competition. The Dutch side, who finished third in the Eredivisie last season, will need to regroup quickly if they are to salvage any pride in the competition. content:

The arrest was announced on Tuesday, September 9, 2026, following the emergence of the fraudulent notice that circulated on social media platforms.

According to the police command, the forged document claimed that OPay was ceasing operations effective immediately, causing panic among users and traders who rely on the platform for financial transactions. The notice, which bore the OPay logo and appeared official, was shared widely across WhatsApp groups and Twitter before the error was detected.

Hafsat Abubakar was paraded alongside other suspects at the command’s headquarters in Abuja. The National Cybercrime Centre traced the origin of the document to her, stating that she created the fake notice with the intent to cause public panic and tarnish the reputation of the fintech firm. The police said investigations revealed that the motive was not financial gain but rather to create confusion in the digital payment space.

OPay Nigeria Limited released a statement on the same day denying that it was shutting down. The company said it remained fully operational and that its services were functioning normally. The firm thanked the police for the swift response and urged the public to disregard any unofficial information about its operations.

The arrest comes at a time when digital financial services in Nigeria have seen rapid growth, with OPay among the leading platforms for mobile money, ride-hailing, and food delivery. Cybersecurity experts have warned that the rise of fintech platforms has also attracted individuals seeking to exploit public trust through misinformation. The police command said it would continue to monitor for similar incidents and urged members of the public to verify information through official channels.

Legal analysts noted that the charge against Abubakar could fall under Nigeria’s Cybercrime (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, which prohibits the creation and distribution of forged electronic documents. If convicted, she could face significant penalties including fines and imprisonment. The police have not yet disclosed the specific charges preferred, but said the case would be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others who might consider similar acts.

The Nation Newspaper reported that Lagos State had recorded 53 suspected cases of diphtheria in 2026, including six laboratory-confirmed cases, though this development was unrelated to the OPay arrest. The state government had assured residents that there was no widespread outbreak of the disease.

The investigation into the forged OPay notice remains ongoing. The police said they were examining whether Abubakar acted alone or had collaborators, and whether the fake notice was part of a broader campaign to destabilize digital financial services in the country.

title: AI Agents Are Changing How People Work — And the Shift Is Only Beginning
author: AI News Factory Desk
excerpt: AI agents are moving beyond simple chat interfaces and becoming capable of completing increasingly complex tasks across work and business.
content: Artificial intelligence is entering another phase of its evolution as AI agents become increasingly capable of performing multi-step tasks rather than simply responding to individual prompts.

The change matters because agents can potentially connect reasoning with actions. Instead of asking a system a question and manually carrying out the result, users can increasingly delegate parts of a workflow to software.

Businesses are watching the development closely as companies explore how agentic systems could assist with research, customer service, software development, analysis and other knowledge-intensive work.
The technology remains imperfect. Reliability, security, privacy and the ability to verify automated decisions remain important challenges.
For users, the larger story is not simply about smarter chatbots. It is about software becoming more capable of taking action on a person's behalf.

title: The Global Technology Shift Everyone Should Be Watching
author: AI News Factory Desk
excerpt: Technology is becoming increasingly embedded in everyday infrastructure, changing how people communicate, work and access information.
content: Technology is no longer limited to the devices people carry. Increasingly, software and connected systems are becoming part of the infrastructure behind everyday life.
Cloud computing, artificial intelligence, automation and increasingly capable connected devices are reshaping the way organisations operate.
The pace of change also creates new questions around security, privacy and access.
For consumers and businesses alike, understanding these shifts may become as important as adopting the technology itself.

title: What AI Could Mean for the Next Business Cycle
author: AI News Factory Business Desk
excerpt: Companies are increasingly treating artificial intelligence as an operational technology rather than simply an experimental tool.
content: Artificial intelligence is becoming a strategic consideration for businesses across industries.
The focus is gradually moving from experimentation toward practical questions about productivity, costs, customer experience and competitive advantage.
That transition could make the coming years important for companies deciding where AI should be deployed and where human oversight must remain central.
The strongest results may come from organisations that treat AI as part of a broader operating strategy rather than as a standalone technology.

title: Why Scientific Discoveries Still Matter in a Fast-Moving World
author: AI News Factory Science Desk
excerpt: Scientific research continues to shape medicine, technology and our understanding of the world around us.
content: Scientific progress rarely happens overnight. Many major advances emerge from years of experiments, observations and incremental discoveries.
That process can make science difficult to communicate in a world increasingly driven by rapid news cycles.
Yet the implications of scientific research can extend far beyond the original discovery, influencing medicine, engineering, environmental policy and future technologies.
Understanding the evidence behind a discovery is therefore just as important as understanding the headline.

title: How Information Shapes the Modern World
author: AI News Factory World Desk
excerpt: The speed at which information travels is changing how societies understand events as they happen.
content: Information now travels across borders within seconds, creating unprecedented access to events happening around the world.
That speed has advantages, but it also creates challenges. Early reports can change as additional evidence becomes available.
For readers, distinguishing between confirmed information, developing reports and speculation is increasingly important.
A modern newsroom therefore has to do more than publish quickly. It must also provide context and clearly communicate uncertainty.
